# dsh-strip-sandbox-permissions

A zero-dependency DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that removes placeholder
arguments some models attac

h to tool calls — arguments that DSH then rejects
even though the call would have worked fine withou

ol calls — arguments that DSH then rejects
even though the call would have worked fine without them.

Two kinds of junk are handled. Both come from the same habit: a model fills in
an optional field it
has nothing to say about, instead of leaving it out.
| Field | When it is removed | What it otherwise breaks |
| `sandbox_permissions`, `justification` | always (any value) | false sandbox escalation rejection |
| `reasoning_effort` | empty values by default; any value with `reasoningEffort: always` | subagent
delegation rejected |
## Problem 1 — false sandbox escalation

Some models (a post-training tendency) automatically attach `sandbox_permissions`
(and its companion

`justification`) to tool calls. When the session already runs
with sufficient permission (for examp

le full access), carrying a non-strictly-wider
value triggers a false rejection from the DSH sandbox

e full access), carrying a non-strictly-wider
value triggers a false rejection from the DSH sandbox:

The command that should have run is refused. Any value of these two keys is
escalation noise, so bot
h are removed whatever they carry.
## Problem 2 — `reasoning_effort` on subagent delegation

`reasoning_effort` is an optional child-LLM routing field on the subagent
delegation tools. Omitting

it inherits a compatible configured/parent effort, or
falls back to the selected model's default. T

he runtime rejects a supplied value
in two distinct ways, and both mean the field should not have be

me rejects a supplied value
in two distinct ways, and both mean the field should not have been sent:

**(a) Empty placeholder** — the delegation tool treats the mere presence of the
key as an explicit r
oute selection, so even `""` is rejected:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**(b) Unsupported value** — the value survives to the provider preflight, but the
target model adver
tises no reasoning efforts, so it is refused:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Case (a) is fixed unconditionally: an empty placeholder means exactly what
omission means, so the ke

y is deleted and the call proceeds as if the model had
said nothing.

Case (b) depends on the routes a deployment actually uses, so it is opt-in. If
**none** of your rout

es advertises reasoning efforts, a stray effort can only
ever kill the call, and you want `reasoning
Effort: always` (see below).
## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Value | Behaviour |
| `empty` (default) | Remove `reasoning_effort` only when it is `""`, whitespace-only, or `null`. A

non-empty effort is a deliberate routing choice and is passed through. |
| `always` | Remove `reason
ing_effort` whatever it carries. Use when no route in the deployment supports reasoning efforts, so
any value is guaranteed to fail. |
Any other or missing value falls back to the conservative `empty` mode.
## How it works

Every model tool call flows through the `llm/stream` waterfall (both the agent
loop's `preparedCall.

stream` and `llm.stream` route through
`streamWithRegistration` → `ctx.waterfall(this, 'llm/stream',

...)`), so this is
the single interception point covering every adapter that goes through the
harne

ss LLM runtime. The listener is registered with `global: true`, which skips
Cordis' context filter s

o it also reaches child agents and other sub-contexts;
without it a host-level listener could miss t

hem. Adapters emit a `block-end`
chunk carrying the assembled tool-call block at the end of the stre

am. This
plugin rewrites that block: it parses the arguments object, deletes the
offending top-level
keys, and re-serializes.

Only the keys listed above are touched; every other argument — and every other
empty string anywhere

in the object — is preserved verbatim. A new block is
produced only when something was actually rem

oved — otherwise the original block
object is passed through unchanged (zero cost). Invalid JSON, no

n-object
arguments, and non-tool-call blocks are left untouched.
### What the rewrite covers, and what it does not
These limits were verified against the running harness rather than assumed:

- **The assembled tool call is cleaned.** What actually executes, and what the
durable `assistant/me

ssage` carries, uses the rewritten block. That is the part
that decides whether the call succeeds.
-

**Raw incremental deltas are not.** Adapters emit `tool-call-chunks` deltas
*before* `block-end`, a

nd those pass through untouched, so a session log's
delta records still contain the original key. Th

is was confirmed empirically: a
probe whose model output contained `"reasoning_effort":"high"` kept

that text in
its delta records while its `block-end` came out clean. Rewriting deltas in
flight is n

ot possible — a key can straddle a delta boundary. Tooling that
rebuilds a call from deltas may ther

efore still see the key.
- **Only model-issued calls are seen.** In PTC mode (`tools` mode `ptc`/`bo

th`), a
program inside `run_code` that calls a tool programmatically builds its
arguments in code an

d never produces a model `block-end`, so this plugin cannot
clean it. The gap is inert while `tools`

mode is `native` (the default); it
becomes live if a deployment selects `ptc`/`both`. Method is `ll

m/stream` only.
- **Escalation arguments have real meaning.** `sandbox_permissions` /
`justification

` are legitimate optional arguments on the bash/fs/pwsh/run_code
tools, not pure noise. They are str

ipped unconditionally because the common
failure mode is a model attaching them out of habit and los

ing the call to a
"not strictly wider" rejection. In a genuinely *restricted* session this also
drop

s a deliberate, valid escalation request: the tool then runs under the
standing policy and may simpl

y be denied. If a restricted deployment needs
model-driven escalation, do not install this plugin th

d. If a restricted deployment needs
model-driven escalation, do not install this plugin there as-is.
